visual: Compact grey-green mound with abundant rose-pink, lightly fringed flowers over a long season.
water: Moderate; water during establishment and prolonged dry spells, allowing excess water to drain.
soil: Fertile to moderately fertile, neutral to alkaline, well-drained soil.
soilWarning: Avoid winter waterlogging and heavy, persistently wet ground.
prune: Deadhead regularly to prolong flowering; trim lightly after the main flush to keep plants compact.
cvs: Retail colour selection sold as 'Hardy Rose'
hardinessNote: Marketed as a hardy perennial Dianthus; exact cultivar identity and therefore precise hardiness are not published.
resilience: Compact and generally easy once established; good drainage is more important than rich soil.
uses: Containers, edging, sunny borders, rock gardens and pollinator planting.
uncertain: 'Hardy Rose' appears to be a retail colour/marketing name rather than a traceable registered cultivar; species or hybrid parentage was not confirmed.

visual: Low, bushy grey-green foliage carrying rich violet-purple, fringed flowers from spring into late summer.
water: Moderate; water during establishment and in dry spells, but do not keep constantly wet.
soil: Fertile to moderately fertile, neutral to alkaline, well-drained soil.
soilWarning: Avoid winter waterlogging and dense, poorly drained clay.
prune: Deadhead spent flowers and shear lightly after flowering to encourage a tidy second flush.
cvs: Retail colour selection sold as 'Hardy Violet'
hardinessNote: Sold as a hardy perennial Dianthus, but no cultivar-level hardiness record was located.
resilience: Tolerates exposed sunny positions once rooted where drainage is sharp.
uses: Containers, edging, rock gardens, sunny borders and pollinator planting.
uncertain: 'Hardy Violet' is sold as a colour selection without a confirmed botanical cultivar denomination; species or hybrid parentage remains unresolved.

visual: Compact blue-green foliage with violet flowers edged or patterned in a contrasting picotee margin.
water: Moderate; water in dry spells but allow the root zone to drain freely.
soil: Moderately fertile, neutral to alkaline, sharply well-drained soil.
soilWarning: Avoid winter wet and deep planting around the crown.
prune: Deadhead regularly and trim back lightly after the main flowering flush.
cvs: Retail colour selection sold as 'Hardy Violet Picotee'
hardinessNote: Treated as a hardy bedding/perennial Dianthus; exact cultivar-level hardiness is unverified.
resilience: Best longevity comes from sun, airflow and free drainage.
uses: Containers, edging, rock gardens, sunny borders and pollinator planting.
uncertain: No authoritative cultivar record was located for the exact retail name 'Hardy Violet Picotee'; do not merge it with a named picotee cultivar without a label or breeder code.

visual: Low evergreen groundcover with glossy dark green leaves narrowly edged creamy white and large vivid violet flowers.
water: Moderate; keep from drying out during establishment and prolonged summer drought.
soil: Any reasonably fertile soil, moist to well drained, acid to alkaline.
soilWarning: Avoid very dry ground; spreading shoots can root and become difficult to contain.
prune: Cut back unwanted runners in early spring and divide congested growth when needed.
toxicity: Harmful if eaten; Vinca contains biologically active alkaloids.
hardinessNote: RHS H6; hardy throughout the UK and northern Europe.
resilience: Very shade tolerant, cold hardy and adaptable once established.
uses: Ground cover, banks, woodland edges, underplanting shrubs and difficult shaded sites.

visual: Mat-forming evergreen with glossy dark green leaves and clean white, five-petalled flowers from spring into summer.
water: Moderate; keep evenly moist while establishing and water during prolonged drought.
soil: Any reasonably fertile, moist but well-drained soil; acid, neutral or alkaline.
soilWarning: Avoid very dry soil and control rooting runners if spread is unwanted.
prune: Cut back hard in early spring if needed to restrict spread and refresh growth.
toxicity: Harmful if eaten; Vinca contains biologically active alkaloids.
hardinessNote: RHS H6; fully hardy in UK conditions.
resilience: Cold hardy, adaptable and useful in sun or shade once established.
uses: Ground cover, banks, woodland edges, containers and underplanting shrubs.
uncertain: RHS currently lists the cultivar name as unresolved, although 'Colada' is established in horticultural trade.

visual: Trailing pinkish stems densely set with tiny rounded silvery grey-green leaves, making a soft cascading houseplant.
water: Moderate; keep lightly moist in active growth, letting the surface dry slightly between waterings.
aspect: Bright indirect light to partial shade
soil: Airy, moisture-retentive but free-draining houseplant compost.
soilWarning: Avoid waterlogging, cold draughts and strong direct midday sun.
prune: Pinch growing tips to encourage a dense, bushy trailing habit.
hardinessNote: RHS H1A; keep as a warm houseplant year-round.
resilience: Generally easy indoors with steady warmth and moderate humidity.
uses: Houseplants, hanging pots, shelves, terrariums and mixed indoor displays.
uncertain: RHS lists the name status as unresolved, but the cultivar is consistently traded as Pilea glaucophylla 'Greyzy'.

visual: Compact upright houseplant with glossy fleshy green leaves broadly margined cream, often with a soft pink-red rim.
water: Low to moderate; water thoroughly, then allow the upper compost to dry before watering again.
soil: Open, free-draining peat-free houseplant compost with added mineral drainage.
soilWarning: Overwatering is the main risk; avoid cold wet roots and harsh direct sun.
prune: Pinch or trim leggy shoots to maintain a compact rounded habit.
hardinessNote: Tender tropical houseplant; best kept above about 15°C.
resilience: Fleshy leaves tolerate short dry periods; average household humidity is usually adequate.
uses: Houseplants, desks, shelves, small pots and mixed foliage displays.

visual: Low creeping succulent with green-centred leaves edged cream and pink, plus clusters of pale pink starry summer flowers.
water: Low; water while establishing, then only during prolonged dry spells.
soil: Moderately fertile, neutral to alkaline, sharply well-drained soil.
soilWarning: Avoid winter waterlogging; green reversions can outgrow the variegated shoots and should be removed.
prune: No routine pruning; remove reverted green shoots and trim untidy growth after flowering.
cvs: syn. Phedimus spurius 'Tricolor'; commonly sold as Sedum spurium 'Tricolor'
hardinessNote: RHS H5 for the variegated form.
resilience: Drought tolerant once established and well suited to poor, stony ground.
uses: Rock gardens, gravel gardens, edging, ground cover, walls and containers.
uncertain: RHS accepts 'Tricolor' as the common trade name but lists Sedum spurium 'Variegatum' as the cultivar name; Phedimus spurius 'Tricolor' is a botanical synonym.

visual: Mounded bright red foliage deepening to wine-red through summer, with airy pink-and-white flowers on dark red stems.
water: Moderate; maintain even moisture without leaving the crown waterlogged.
soil: Fertile, moist but well-drained neutral soil.
soilWarning: Avoid winter waterlogging and burying the crown; mulch around rather than over the crown.
prune: Remove faded flower spikes and tidy damaged foliage in late winter or early spring.
hardinessNote: RHS H6; hardy throughout the UK.
resilience: Cold hardy and drought resistant once established where drainage is good.
uses: Containers, edging, ground cover, mixed borders, cut flowers and foliage contrast.

visual: Compact mound of pink-gold foliage washed with a silvery veil, topped by cream flowers on maroon stems.
water: Moderate; keep evenly moist but well drained.
soil: Fertile, neutral to slightly acid, moist but well-drained soil.
soilWarning: Protect pale foliage from hot scorching sun and avoid winter waterlogging.
prune: Remove faded flower spikes and old leaves; divide every few years to maintain vigour.
hardinessNote: RHS H6; hardy throughout the UK.
resilience: Cold hardy and reported by RHS as drought resistant once established.
uses: Containers, edging, ground cover, mixed borders and shaded foliage planting.
uncertain: RHS treats 'Champagne' as a synonym/trade presentation associated with cultivar denomination 'Tnheucha'.

visual: Dense mound of glossy, deeply lobed intense purple leaves, with short spikes of purple-pink summer flowers.
water: Moderate; keep evenly moist during establishment and dry weather.
soil: Fertile, neutral, moist but well-drained soil.
soilWarning: Avoid winter waterlogging; mulch annually as the crown can rise above soil level.
prune: Deadhead flower stems and remove old or damaged foliage.
hardinessNote: RHS H5; hardy in most UK gardens.
resilience: Cold hardy and drought resistant once established; strong foliage colour in good light.
uses: Containers, edging, ground cover, mixed borders and bold foliage contrast.

visual: Compact mound of purple leaves heavily overlaid with metallic silver, topped by loose sprays of brick-red flowers.
water: Moderate; keep evenly moist but ensure excellent drainage around the crown.
soil: Fertile, neutral, moist but well-drained soil.
soilWarning: Avoid winter waterlogging and prolonged severe drought.
prune: Remove faded flower spikes and tidy damaged foliage in late winter.
hardinessNote: RHS H6; hardy throughout the UK.
resilience: Cold hardy and drought resistant once established where drainage is good.
uses: Containers, edging, mixed borders, ground cover and metallic foliage contrast.

visual: Bright yellow, deeply cut foliage marked by a bold dark red centre, with airy white flowers in spring.
water: Moderate; keep consistently moist but never waterlogged.
soil: Fertile, neutral, moist but well-drained loam or sandy soil.
soilWarning: Avoid stagnant winter wet and hot exposed sites that scorch the yellow foliage.
prune: Remove faded flower spikes and damaged leaves; lift and replant if the crown rises.
hardinessNote: RHS H6; hardy throughout the UK.
resilience: Cold hardy and shade tolerant; performs best with consistent moisture and good drainage.
uses: Shade borders, containers, edging, ground cover and bright foliage contrast.

visual: Lacy green leaves with burgundy markings beneath upright, foamy pink-to-white flower spikes in spring and early summer.
water: Moderate to high; keep cool and consistently moist without waterlogging.
soil: Humus-rich, fertile, moist but well-drained soil.
soilWarning: Avoid prolonged drought and excessive winter wet around the crown.
prune: Deadhead after flowering and remove old or damaged leaves in late winter or early spring.
hardinessNote: RHS AGM listing gives H6; hardy throughout the UK and northern Europe.
resilience: Cold hardy, shade tolerant and reliable in cool, humus-rich soils.
uses: Woodland gardens, shaded borders, ground cover, underplanting and containers.

visual: Compact, rounded evergreen shrub with pointed green leaves and dense red-pink flower clusters from summer into autumn.
water: Moderate; keep evenly moist while establishing and do not allow containers to dry out completely.
soil: Moist but well-drained, moderately fertile soil.
soilWarning: Protect from hard frost and avoid cold, exposed, waterlogged sites.
prune: Trim lightly just below spent flower heads after flowering to maintain the rounded shape.
hardinessNote: UK grower guidance says protect from frost; best treated as a tender to borderline-hardy Hebe in colder gardens.
resilience: Compact and long-flowering, but less frost tolerant than many hardy Hebe cultivars.
uses: Patio containers, seasonal colour, sheltered borders and pollinator planting.
uncertain: Addenda markets Petita Red as a branded colour selection; an underlying cultivar denomination was not located.
Published UK grower guidance says 'protect from frost', so the H3 score is a cautious practical estimate rather than an RHS cultivar rating.

visual: Trailing or climbing evergreen vine with glossy heart-shaped green leaves splashed and streaked yellow or cream.
water: Moderate; water when the upper compost has partly dried and reduce watering in winter.
aspect: Bright indirect light to partial shade
soil: Free-draining, fertile peat-free houseplant compost.
soilWarning: Avoid overwatering, cold draughts and deep shade, which reduces variegation.
prune: Tip prune in spring or trim long vines at any time during active growth to encourage branching.
toxicity: Harmful if eaten; sap can irritate skin and eyes and is toxic to pets.
hardinessNote: RHS H1B; keep frost-free and preferably warm indoors.
resilience: Very adaptable houseplant that tolerates lower light and short dry periods better than many tropical climbers.
uses: Houseplants, hanging pots, shelves, moss poles and indoor green walls.
uncertain: The supplied label 'Epipremnum pinnatum Golden Pothos' maps to RHS Epipremnum aureum; RHS lists E. pinnatum 'Aureum' as a synonym rather than 'Golden Pothos' as a cultivar.

visual: Upright tropical foliage plant with glossy arrow-shaped green leaves on striking zebra-striped pale-and-dark petioles.
water: Moderate to high; keep evenly moist in active growth, then reduce sharply in winter.
soil: Peat-free houseplant compost with added grit or other free-draining mineral material.
soilWarning: Avoid cold wet compost, direct scorching sun and temperatures below about 15°C.
prune: No routine pruning; remove yellow or damaged leaves cleanly at the base.
toxicity: Toxic if eaten; sap can irritate skin and eyes and is toxic to pets.
hardinessNote: RHS H1A; maintain above 15°C.
resilience: Can shed older leaves naturally; recovers well with warmth, humidity and steady moisture.
uses: Houseplants, conservatories and bold tropical foliage displays.

visual: Upright branching shrub with dense whorls of narrow deep green leaves edged broad yellow-green.
water: Moderate; water during growth once the surface starts to dry and water sparingly in winter.
soil: Peat-free loam-based houseplant compost with good drainage.
soilWarning: Avoid waterlogging, harsh midday sun, cold draughts and repeated watering with very hard tap water.
prune: Usually none; shorten weak or overlong stems in spring to encourage branching.
hardinessNote: RHS H1B; frost tender and best kept above 10°C.
resilience: Slow-growing, durable and tolerant of normal indoor humidity once established.
uses: Houseplants, offices, conservatories and architectural foliage displays.
uncertain: RHS lists the cultivar name as not established, although it is widely and consistently traded as 'Song of India'.

visual: Arching fountain of narrow green leaves with clean white margins, producing white flowers and dangling plantlets.
water: Moderate; water regularly in growth but let excess drain and reduce watering in winter.
aspect: Bright indirect light to partial shade
soil: Peat-free multipurpose or houseplant compost, moist but well drained.
soilWarning: Avoid prolonged waterlogging and strong hot sun that can scorch the pale leaf margins.
prune: No pruning required; remove brown leaves and unwanted runners or plantlets.
hardinessNote: RHS H2; frost tender, though tolerant of cool indoor conditions.
resilience: Very adaptable and tolerant of variable light, missed waterings and ordinary indoor conditions.
uses: Houseplants, hanging baskets, shelves, offices and easy propagation displays.

visual: Dense rosette of glossy, leathery dark green fronds divided into fine feathery segments, often producing plantlets.
water: Moderate to high; keep compost lightly and consistently moist without leaving roots waterlogged.
aspect: Bright indirect light to partial shade
soil: Humus-rich, moisture-retentive but well-drained peat-free houseplant compost.
soilWarning: Avoid direct hot sun, dry radiator air, cold draughts and allowing the root ball to dry completely.
prune: Remove old or damaged fronds at the base; avoid damaging emerging fronds.
hardinessNote: Best kept warm indoors; RHS lists it as a houseplant cultivar and specialist growers recommend temperatures around or above 15°C.
resilience: More tolerant of average indoor humidity than many delicate ferns, but performs best with steady moisture.
uses: Houseplants, bathrooms, kitchens, conservatories, shelves and lush foliage displays.
uncertain: Parentage is commonly given in trade as Asplenium difforme × A. dimorphum, while RHS currently lists the accepted name simply as Asplenium 'Parvati'.

visual: Bushy tropical shrub with leathery green leaves boldly veined and splashed yellow, orange, red and pink.
water: Moderate to high; keep evenly moist in active growth while allowing free drainage.
soil: Peat-free loam-based or ericaceous houseplant compost, moist but well drained.
soilWarning: Avoid cold draughts, dry air, hard drying of the compost and strong summer sun.
prune: Prune leggy stems in spring if needed; wear gloves because the sap can irritate skin.
toxicity: Harmful if eaten; latex-like sap can irritate skin and eyes.
hardinessNote: RHS H1B; keep warm and frost-free, ideally above about 15°C.
resilience: Colour is best with bright light, warmth and humidity; prone to leaf drop if conditions change abruptly.
uses: Houseplants, conservatories and high-colour tropical foliage displays.
uncertain: RHS currently marks Codiaeum variegatum var. pictum 'Petra' as unresolved; the plant is also widely sold as Codiaeum variegatum 'Petra'.

visual: Elegant weeping evergreen with slender branches and glossy dark green leaves broadly and irregularly margined creamy white.
water: Moderate; water when the surface begins to dry, then reduce watering in winter.
soil: Fertile, well-drained houseplant compost.
soilWarning: Avoid waterlogging, cold draughts and sudden changes in position or light, which can trigger leaf drop.
prune: Trim in spring or summer to maintain shape and remove weak or congested growth.
toxicity: Harmful if eaten; milky sap may cause skin allergy or irritation and can affect pets.
hardinessNote: RHS H1C; frost tender and best grown as a houseplant.
resilience: Long-lived indoors but sensitive to sudden environmental changes; tolerates pruning well.
uses: Houseplants, conservatories, offices, specimen pots and variegated foliage displays.
uncertain: RHS lists the cultivar name status as unresolved, although 'Twilight' is well established in the houseplant trade.
